items.title: Bela Fleck interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, December 7, 2004
items.q: we loved the fact that there are tapes of Charlie Parker

ctx.x: Was it a hard decision to basically allow and almost encourage people to tape you in your concerts?

No, I mean I think we just decided to do it right at the beginning, that we just decided to allow it. And it was a time when that was sort of starting to happen. And I guess Phish was an example to me. They were starting to build a huge audience and they were allowing taping and that seemed to be part of it, the Grateful Dead thing the whole sort of jam band thing was just starting. And it seemed like a neat thing to do. And plus we were all, being musicians that study a lot of a old music, we loved the fact that…
anything that encourages the live touring base, if you enjoy playing and you like going out and touring, then it’s a wiser business plan with more longevity.
